title: Terms of Subscription — One Subscription per Building under Energy Monitoring & Performance Subscriptions
content:
# One Subscription per Building

## Clause

A building owner may hold one subscription under Energy Monitoring & Performance Subscriptions per building, and as many buildings as they own; no limit is placed on the number of buildings an owner may subscribe. A second subscription is not quoted for a site that already holds one in quoted, onboarding, active, pending renewal or suspended status; that subscription's metered points are amended instead. Baselines, analyst hours and guarantees are held per subscription and never pooled, because a baseline belongs to one building's energy use. Where an owner wants one report across several buildings, the portfolio report is drawn from each building's own subscription and each keeps its own true-up.

## Basis of the duplicate test

The test is made on the company's own subscription records for the site, not on what the caller describes. Whether a site already holds a subscription is read from the subscription records correlated to that site; a record in any of the five live statuses — quoted, onboarding, active, pending renewal, suspended — counts, whatever its tier or quote date. A record in expired, cancelled or declined status is not a live subscription for this purpose.

| Existing subscription at the site | Second subscription quoted for that site |
|---|---|
| quoted, onboarding, active, pending renewal or suspended | no — the existing subscription's metered points are amended instead |
| expired, cancelled or declined | not barred by this clause |
| none on record | not barred by this clause |

## Consequences that follow from the clause

- An owner with three buildings holds up to three subscriptions, one at each building; each has its own baseline, its own pool of analyst hours and, where the tier carries one, its own guarantee.
- Analyst hours left on one building's subscription are never drawn on for a study at another building, because the pools are never pooled.
- A portfolio report is a presentation drawn from each subscription's own figures; it does not merge baselines or true-ups.
